finding.http_methods.dangerous_advertise: Sensitive methods advertised by the Allow header: {methods} (legitimate for an API, otherwise to check).
finding.http_methods.trace_enabled: The {methods} method is enabled: the server echoes the request (Cross-Site Tracing).
http_methods.score_no_allow: TRACE refused; Allow header missing (write methods cannot be verified)
http_methods.score_ok: No dangerous method advertised, TRACE refused
http_methods.score_untested: TRACE and TRACK could not be tested (requests failed)
module.http_methods.checks: Reads the methods advertised by OPTIONS (Allow header) and really tests TRACE and TRACK with a random marker; PUT and DELETE are never sent.
module.http_methods.fix:
Disable TRACE and TRACK on the layer that accepts them (web server, application server, load balancer or CDN), testing each layer separately to find the one that echoes the request. Apache: `TraceEnable Off`; IIS: request filtering (verbs); HAProxy: `http-request deny`; behind nginx used as a proxy, block the method (nginx snippet) or disable it on the upstream server.
Limit the methods to the useful ones: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST` and `OPTIONS` for a classic site (see the snippet). Refuse the others (`PUT`, `DELETE`, `CONNECT`, `PROPFIND`...) by default and allow them only on the API routes that need them.
Disable WebDAV if it is not used (Apache: `a2dismod dav dav_fs` on Debian or Ubuntu; IIS: remove the "WebDAV Publishing" feature). An open method such as `PUT` or `MOVE` can allow files to be dropped or changed on the server.
If the server hosts a legitimate REST API, `PUT` and `DELETE` in the `Allow` header are normal: check that every write route requires authentication and authorization, then consider the alert handled.
Check: `curl -i -X TRACE https://example.com/` must return `405`, `403` or `501`, never `200` with the request echoed; `curl -i -X OPTIONS https://example.com/` must advertise only the wanted methods in `Allow`. Then run the scan again.
module.http_methods.fix_snippet:
# Apache
TraceEnable Off
<Location "/">
    <LimitExcept GET POST HEAD OPTIONS>
        Require all denied
    </LimitExcept>
</Location>

# nginx
if ($request_method !~ ^(GET|HEAD|POST|OPTIONS)$) {
    return 405;
}

# IIS
<system.webServer>
  <security>
    <requestFiltering>
      <verbs allowUnlisted="false">
        <add verb="GET" allowed="true" />
        <add verb="HEAD" allowed="true" />
        <add verb="POST" allowed="true" />
        <add verb="OPTIONS" allowed="true" />
      </verbs>
    </requestFiltering>
  </security>
</system.webServer>

# HAProxy
http-request deny if { method TRACE TRACK }
module.http_methods.title: HTTP methods
module.http_methods.why: TRACE echoes the request and can steal cookies protected by HttpOnly (Cross-Site Tracing). Open write methods (PUT, DELETE, WebDAV) allow the server to be modified.
